headline: Excalidraw wins the job. Its Share step is where people hesitate.
lede: Task: sketch a 3-step flowchart and send a teammate a link. Every tester got there on Excalidraw with no account, in 7 to 16 actions. On tldraw it took 30 to 35 actions behind a sign-in wall, and one tester was blocked. On Excalidraw the hesitation is all in sharing.

testers.label: plain-tester
testers.name: Plain tester
testers.who: The usual end-to-end check: methodical, finishes every step, notes anything broken.

testers.label: group-1
testers.name: Product Makers
testers.who: Founders and makers who ship their own launches; 92% have made or hunted a launch. They read a product as builders and care about privacy and integrations.

testers.label: group-2
testers.name: Tech Innovators
testers.who: The most active voters: developers, marketers and PMs who like dev tools and APIs. They look for pricing, limits and integrations before adopting.

testers.label: group-3
testers.name: Curious Observers
testers.who: The largest and least invested group: newer accounts, casual. They want value on the first screen and leave at the first wall.

divergences.title: No account needed is Excalidraw's edge over tldraw, but it is said too quietly to count
divergences.summary: On tldraw all 4 testers hit a sign-in wall to share (12 to 15 extra steps; Makers were blocked). On Excalidraw, 2 of 4 noticed 'no account needed', in small text under the button. Nothing in the main share flow says it plainly.

divergences.title: Live session or read-only link? Testers guessed which one a teammate needs.
divergences.summary: 3 of 4 chose 'Export to Link' and then wondered whether later edits would show. Makers expected a live link like Figma or Loom, which tldraw gives by default ('Anyone with the link: Editor').

divergences.title: The Share button is an icon with no word on it.
divergences.summary: All 4 testers hesitated at the top-right icon and found it by position and colour. Figma, Miro and FigJam all label it 'Share'.

divergences.title: Everyone saw the flowchart shortcut. Makers and Innovators still labelled each box first.
divergences.summary: Observers used Ctrl + arrow straight away and finished in 8 steps. Makers and Innovators read the hint, then labelled box by box and chained after, taking 17. The hint teaches the keys, not the order that saves time.

divergences.title: Innovators looked for pricing, limits and API access, and found nothing.
divergences.summary: Before adopting for a team, Tech Innovators wanted to know how long links last, what Excalidraw+ adds, and whether there is an API. The share flow says none of it.

divergences.title: The style panel covers the canvas while you draw.
divergences.summary: The first box landed half under the panel for Observers; Makers called the panel 'a lot of options' for a box.

variations.title: Put the word 'Share' on the Share button
variations.change: Turn the top-right icon into a labelled button, as Figma, Miro and FigJam do.

variations.title: Make 'no account needed' the headline of the share dialog
variations.change: The dialog says it already, in small grey text under the button, and 2 of 4 testers spotted it. Move it into the heading of the link option, so the gap with tldraw (4 of 4 hit a sign-in wall there) registers as a reason to choose Excalidraw.

variations.evidence: tldraw: 4 of 4 hit a sign-in wall · Excalidraw: 2 of 4 noticed 'no account'

variations.title: Tell people the snapshot won't update
variations.change: In the link dialog, add one line under the link: later edits won't show; start a live session if they should.

variations.evidence: 3 of 4 unsure what a teammate gets

variations.title: Make the flowchart shortcut impossible to miss
variations.change: After the first box is drawn, show a small chip beside it: press Ctrl + → to add the next step. Today the tip is a faint grey line under the toolbar.
variations.evidence: 2 of 4 labelled first and took 2x the steps

variations.title: Spell out what a teammate gets from each option
variations.change: Rename 'Start session' to say what it is (a live link teammates can edit), so people stop guessing between the two.

variations.evidence: 3 of 4 unsure; Makers expected a live link
variations.risk: Starts a live session: needs a privacy check

variations.title: Show what Excalidraw+ adds where people ask
variations.change: Add a small footer to the link dialog: links that last, live team spaces, and the API, with a link to plans.

overlays.label: Need links that last or the API? See Excalidraw+ plans ▸

variations.title: Fold the style panel away while drawing
variations.change: Keep the style panel collapsed to a small tab until someone opens it, so the first box isn't drawn under it.
variations.risk: Hides styling from people who use it

accuracy: Each tester ran once per product (8 live browser runs on Camoufox). The groups describe who these Product Hunt users are. On 276 past launches their simulated reactions covered 65% of the broad points real commenters raised but only about 9% of the exact issues, and how they behave inside a product has not been validated. Treat each split as a hypothesis with a recording you can watch.

highlights.caption: Observers find Ctrl + arrow: a connected box in one keypress.
Every tester stops at the unlabelled Share icon.
Live session or read-only link? The tester guesses.
Link in hand, Makers ask: will my later edits show?
On tldraw the share icon only exports a PNG.
tldraw: sign-in, then a captcha, to get a link.
Makers are blocked: 'Too many verification requests'.

disclosure: The 4 testers are AI agents using the real sites in real browsers. Each group tester's persona is built from the profiles of thousands of real Product Hunt users. One run per tester per product: a fast first pass to choose what to test for real, not a validation.
method: A step is one action (a click, a key press, typing). Opening the page is step 0. 'Got the link' means the tester ended with a shareable link; the Observers' chart had no box labels and still counts.
Real products, real browsers: 8 sessions on excalidraw.com and tldraw.com, in Camoufox on UserSim's own machines, every action and screenshot recorded.

Simulated people: a plain QA tester plus 3 groups clustered from about 93,000 Product Hunt users read in full (activity, launches, comments, topics). 'Built from 6,500 people' means the persona summarises that cluster; it is still one simulated run.
Priority = how many testers hit it × how bad it was (blocked > hesitated > slower > cosmetic), then effort.

Measured accuracy so far: on 276 past launches, simulated group reactions covered 65% of the broad points real commenters raised but about 9% of exact issues. Behaviour inside a product has not been validated yet.
race_title: Actions to a shareable link: Excalidraw took 7 to 16, tldraw 30 to 35 behind a sign-in wall
